audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer said 'Skill' on all seven rows against the content/packet chart of Annie/Annie/Annie/Annie/Annie/Ekko/Ekko. Separately, whys[4] said 'Level 6 favors Ekko' while win[4] on the same page said Annie — the two halves of the same row disagreed inside one layer.
audit.why: Chronobreak at level 6 is 110 seconds and functions mostly as an escape; Annie's stocked stun into Tibbers is the faster kill at that level. Ekko takes over at one and two items, which is what the chart's last two rows say.
audit.corrected: Full sides aligned to the packet chart; whys[4] rewritten to agree with win[4].

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes described Ekko's scaling as generic 'resets' without naming what changes.
audit.why: The real late spike is Chronobreak's cooldown dropping from 110s to 50s — that is what turns one escape into repeated re-entries.
audit.corrected: spikes[3] now states the 50-second figure and keys the bear to his second entry.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's defect note is right: the page never named a single Ekko ability, and three decisive interactions were absent.
audit.why: From missingInteractions: (a) Chronobreak makes him untargetable through the rewind and heals a percentage of the damage received during it — so committing your last damage into the hologram both misses and refunds him; (b) that heal makes Grievous Wounds timing decide extended trades; (c) Parallel Convergence shields him and stuns when he enters his own anomaly, absorbing the exact window Annie's burst needs; (d) Phase Dive ends in an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up, not the dash, is the tell.
audit.corrected: All four written in: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d, breakdown.feeding, spikes[1], spikes[2], mid, late.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number appeared anywhere on the page.
audit.why: The two punishable numbers are Parallel Convergence at 22s rank 1 and Chronobreak at 110s rank 1 — both long enough to define a window.
audit.corrected: Both stated, plus Phase Dive's 325 range as the reason he must enter Annie's 625.

edits.before: Q last-hits refund mana on kill — farm with it for free and let the stun counter tick where he can see it.
edits.after: Q last-hits refund mana — farm free while his only level-1 damage is a 1075-range grenade he has to land.

edits.before: W joins the stack engine: the cone clears and counts. A stocked stun at level 2 already makes him flinch.
edits.after: W joins the stack engine, and Phase Dive is still a level away — he cannot reach you to punish the cone.

edits.before: E shield completes the loop: stack the passive on your own shield safely. Trade only with the stun loaded.
edits.after: Parallel Convergence arms slowly and costs 22s — stand outside the circle and his stun is only a slow.

edits.before: Hold the four-stack glow and watch him orbit at max range — a stocked Annie controls the lane by standing there.
edits.after: Hold the four-stack glow: Phase Dive is only 325 range, so he has to enter your 625 to start anything at all.

edits.before: Tibbers online — Flash-R-W-Q deletes most mids from full health. The lane is now a geometry problem about your Flash range.
edits.after: Tibbers online, and Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 — your one button comes back faster than his escape does at this level.

edits.before: Luden's/Stormsurge spike: the stun-burst math kills through Doran's defenses. Stock, walk forward, win.
edits.after: His first item turns the W stun into a real burst combo; hold the glow and never trade inside the circle.

edits.before: Late Annie flips fights with one button: flash-Tibbers the clump, peel with the bear, and re-stock off the chaos.
edits.after: He resets fights with Chronobreak and picks the re-entry; your one bear answers only one of those attempts.

edits.before: Ekko wins by landing Chronobreak, denying your pattern, and starting the fight your kit wanted ten seconds later.
edits.after: Ekko wins by stunning you inside Parallel Convergence, then rewinding out of the answer with Chronobreak.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Molten Shield like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Ekko Chronobreak: 110s at rank 1 — he is untargetable through the rewind, so hold Ignite and the last Q for where he lands instead of firing into the hologram. - Parallel Convergence is 22s; outside the circle it cannot stun. - Tibbers goes to kill windows only.

edits.before: If Ekko gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Chronobreak extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q refunds and stay relevant through stocked-stun threat.
edits.after: If Ekko gets a kill, buy Oblivion Orb — Chronobreak heals him off the damage you just dealt. Farm with Q refunds from outside his circle and stay relevant through stocked-stun threat.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry the one button — Flash-Tibbers him once Chronobreak is spent; the bear outlives his whole rewind window.

edits.before: Ahead, shrink the lane: hold the glow, zone Ekko off CS by existing, and Flash-Tibbers the recovery attempt — fed Annie ends games at 20.
edits.after: Ahead, shrink the lane: hold the glow, deny CS while his 325-range dash is down, and Flash-Tibbers the recovery attempt — fed Annie ends games at 20.

edits.before: Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: He is untargetable mid-rewind — save the last Q and Ignite for his landing spot, not the hologram. Until it's spent, every commit is a coin flip.

edits.before: At four stacks: walk forward, Q-stun, W, auto, walk away re-stacking off the wave — a guaranteed chunk he answered with nothing.
edits.after: Phase Dive ends in an auto-attack reset — the wind-up, not the dash, is your cue to shield and turn the stun on him.

edits.before: Ekko spends Chronobreak early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Ekko spends Chronobreak early — that is a 110-second window with no rewind.

edits.before: That is Ekko’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Unstacked, his W circle into Phase Dive is simply a free kill.

edits.before: Level 6 favors Ekko: his ultimate grants a genuine burst-and-escape package that finally threatens Annie back.
edits.after: Level 6 favors Annie: Chronobreak is 110s and mostly an escape, while Tibbers plus a stocked stun is a kill.

edits.before: Ekko's early poke from Q is weak and his W stun zone is slow to arm, so Annie's stronger short trades and Pyromania punish any attempt to stand and fight.
edits.after: Timewinder pokes from 1075 but Parallel Convergence takes seconds to arm and costs 22s, so Annie's short trades and Pyromania punish every attempt to stand and fight.

edits.before: Ekko's ultimate finally gives him a real burst combo and a rewind escape, closing much of the early gap Annie built in lane.
edits.after: Chronobreak makes him untargetable and heals a share of the damage you dealt — burst into it and you refund the entire trade.

edits.before: With one item Ekko can chain W-stun into R for a full burst-and-reset that threatens a kill Annie can't easily answer alone.
edits.after: With one item, Parallel Convergence's stun into Timewinder and Phase Dive kills outright — and the shield he gains entering it eats your burst.

edits.before: Fully scaled Ekko is a snowballing assassin who can reset fights with his ultimate repeatedly, outpacing Annie's single-cooldown burst combo.
edits.after: Fully scaled, Chronobreak drops to 50 seconds — he re-enters a fight nearly as often as you have Tibbers, so hold the bear for his second entry.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 clearly favor you: Ekko's early kit is mostly about setting up his stun zone, and his poke damage is low enough that you can freely trade with Disintegrate. From 3-5 keep pressuring — his W has a real cast delay and whiffing it leaves him with almost no answer to your stun-into-Q combo. Push the wave hard in this window and look to roam, since Ekko has very little kill pressure on you before level 6.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 clearly favor you: Ekko's kit is about arming Parallel Convergence, and Timewinder's poke is low enough that you can trade with Disintegrate freely. From 3-5 keep pressuring — the circle takes seconds to arm and costs 22s, so stepping out of it leaves him almost no answer to your stun-into-Q combo. Push the wave hard here and roam, since a 325-range Phase Dive is little kill pressure before 6.

edits.before: Everything changes at 6: his ultimate is a genuine burst-and-escape tool that can punish you for overextending and gives him a reset if the kill doesn't land outright. Respect his all-in the moment he hits level 6, especially if he's landed a W stun recently — keep your own Pyromania stun ready to answer his engage. If you built a lead in the early levels, keep playing safe rather than looking for extended fights, since his power only grows from here.
edits.after: Everything changes at 6: Chronobreak makes him untargetable through the rewind and heals a portion of the damage you just dealt, so emptying your combo into it refunds the whole trade. Respect the all-in the moment he hits 6, especially with Parallel Convergence armed — keep Pyromania ready to answer the engage and hold Ignite until he lands. If you built an early lead, keep farming instead of hunting extended fights.

edits.before: A scaled Ekko becomes a real snowball threat: W-stun into R burst can delete squishies, and the rewind lets him escape reprisals or reset a losing fight. Annie's stun-Tibbers combo is still strong but is a single-use cooldown, while Ekko's kit rewards patience and repeated engages. Ward the jungle entrances he roams through and try to force fights before he gets a second full item online — the later this goes, the more the matchup favors him.
edits.after: A scaled Ekko is a real snowball threat: a Parallel Convergence stun into Timewinder and Phase Dive deletes squishies, and a 50-second Chronobreak escapes the reprisal or undoes a lost fight. Annie's stun-Tibbers is still strong but it is one 100-second cooldown against his repeated entries. Ward the entrances he roams through, buy Grievous Wounds, and force fights before his second item lands — the later this goes, the more it favors him.

notes: Packet defect confirmed: not one Ekko ability was named anywhere on the page. All five are now used by their real names. Intra-layer contradiction found and fixed: whys[4] said level 6 favors Ekko while win[4] on the same page said Annie. Highest-value addition is Chronobreak's untargetable window plus its heal-off-damage-received — the page previously told you to 'track the hologram' without saying that burst fired into it is both wasted and converted into his healing.
